text: Dear Alan. We need to talk about your router.
Jev made decision models the main character on tech Twitter.
Then Laya went open source. So we taught it to learn.
Here's the problem. Coding agents send every single call to a giant model. Even the easy ones. That's slow.
Meet Pennywise. A reinforcement-learning router that picks the right model for every request.
First, we asked three open models nine hundred forty-eight questions, and graded every answer automatically.
Then Laya learned from the results. A supervised warm start, then REINFORCE. Right answers get rewarded. Waste gets punished.
Here's the policy reshaping itself as it trains. Powered by one very warm laptop.
Using it takes one line: your base URL. Pennywise sits in front of your models and routes every call.
For agents, it checks every tool call. When the fast model fumbles, it escalates. No drama.
Now, Alan. Pennywise is on npm. One custom connector, and every Alan agent can call the router as a tool.
Here's an Alan agent calling it, live. Medium tier, decided in a third of a second, right on the laptop.
So we opened the Alan desktop app, and raced Alan Code's built-in Auto Router.
Same ten coding tasks. Same tests. Go.
Pennywise: eleven minutes. Auto Router: thirty-seven. Both, ten for ten.
Every number is in a nine-page technical report. Confidence intervals included.
It's live, it's open source, and it's one npx command away.
Pennywise. Built for Alan's router. Your move, Alan.
